title: 23.7 BROCA: A 52.4-to-559.2mW Mobile Social Agent System-on-Chip with Adaptive Bit-Truncate Unit and Acoustic-Cluster Bit Grouping
problem: On-device conversational AI requires integrating multimodal perception (speech/vision), retrieval-augmented generation, language modeling, emotion generation, and voice synthesis in power-constrained mobile devices while maintaining quality.
motivation: Personalized mobile agents with human-like conversational capability require on-device AI; cloud-based AI has latency and privacy concerns.
method: BROCA is a single integrated circuit that runs conversational AI directly on mobile devices. It processes conversation through five stages: perceiving user input (with multimodal encoding for speech and vision), retrieving relevant context, generating a response using a transformer language model, generating emotional tone, and converting to speech via a vocoder. To reduce power consumption, the chip uses adaptive bit-truncation and acoustic-cluster bit grouping—techniques that adjust the numerical precision (number of bits) used in each stage based on what that stage actually needs.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using an adaptive bit-truncate unit and acoustic-cluster bit grouping to optimize numerical precision in each stage of the conversational AI pipeline, reducing power consumption.
contributions: 52.4-559.2mW power range across all four AI stages
Adaptive bit-truncation for per-module precision optimization
Acoustic-cluster bit grouping for efficient speech/emotion representations
Integrated multimodal encoder, RAG, language model, emotion classifier, and vocoder
primary_theme: Power-efficient on-device conversational AI SoC with adaptive quantization
